title: Randy and The fumblers: Three Straight Playoff Trips, Still Chasing the Bowl
body: Few managers in the Buckaroo Football League have been as reliably dangerous as Randy. He has run The fumblers since the league's first kickoff in 2023, made the playoffs in each of the first three seasons, and has never finished last. The one thing missing is a Buckaroo Bowl ring.

The 2023 debut was a study in balance: a 7-7 record, 1,462.9 points, the 3 seed, and a third-place finish. It also produced the worst week of his career, a 73.1-point dud against Kaushal in week 6. In 2024 he climbed to 8-6 and the 2 seed, then posted his career-best 162.5 in week 3 against Ramon, a game Brucie surely still remembers. The playoffs were less kind, and he slid to fourth.

Then came 2025, his finest season. The fumblers went 9-7, piled up a career-high 1,792.1 points, grabbed the 2 seed again, and marched all the way to Buckaroo Bowl III, where Sonny's worst-to-first Ben Dover took the crown and left Randy as runner-up. That makes his playoff record 1-3, a stat that says plenty about how often he gets there and how stubborn the last step has been. His points total has gone up every single season, so the engine keeps getting stronger.

As a manager, Randy works the waiver wire harder every year: 5 pickups in 2023, then 10, then 16, and already 14 this season. The trade market is another story. He made zero deals in his first two seasons and has finally made one in each of the last two, which for Randy feels like a seismic shift. Pry a Bears player off his roster and you deserve a plaque. In the head-to-head ledger he owns Ramon (7-4), edges Kaushal (6-5), sits dead even with Kai (6-6), and is a perfect 1-0 against both JMoney and Zoe, giving him early bragging rights in the Bears-Packers department. His problem children are Philly, who leads him 8-5, and Sonny, who holds a 5-3 edge on top of that Bowl III result.

Right now the 2026 season is a grind. The fumblers sit at 3-4 with 752.4 points, and the projections give them just a 3 percent shot at the title. History says don't count him out, because Randy has made a career of being in the mix when it matters. But if this is going to be the year the Bowl finally comes home, the climb starts now.
